annotation.coverageReview: Actually inspected all six original survey views, individual original front and final four-patch overlays. One Capybara head with small eyes, broad rounded snout, brown nose and lower mouth, blue headband and branch crest. Repicked side jaw forward from fabric then expanded for sparse battle mesh; patch includes lower cheek boundary and must be diagnosed before repair. Long ties, neck cloth, folded hands, torso, feet and short tail need full-body review.

Corrected hit reaction keeps forearms below mouth without face penetration. Branch crest, headband ties, tunic, arms, feet and short tail remain connected through attacks, jump and death.

region.finding: All 24 source/battle front/side whole-face and body slices actually inspected across 13 clips at six phases. Capybara face visibly squashes, elongates and changes eye shape in alternate idle, gallop, attack, hit reaction, death and victory. Hit reaction folds the forehead toward the nose and stretches the lower face. Both qualities fail. Antlers, ears, gloves, tunic, legs and feet remain attached. Separate candidate targets measured non-head face influences with a smooth neck fade. Independent anatomy, full-body geometry, conservation and actual visual inspection required before promotion. Candidate v1 rejected by actual visual inspection despite clean numerical checks: raised forearm/collar breaks into jagged panels near the cheek during hit reaction. V2 raises the lower face fade boundary to preserve more of the moving forearm and tunic, while retaining the measured face core. Full repeated review required. Candidate v2 rejected for three body warnings; measured forearm vertices at envelope y -0.18 to -0.21 were still inside the fade. V3 excludes those forearm vertices by starting the fade at -0.17, retaining the face core above -0.13. Full geometry and actual visual review remain required. Candidate v3 rejected for 33 narrow transition warnings. V4 separates the forward chin depth fade from the higher cheek fade, using measured chin depth above 0.859 and side-jaw height above -0.084. The measured forearm y -0.18 to -0.21 and z 0.64 to 0.70 stays outside both regions; no topology or motion changes. Candidate v4 rejected for ten transition warnings. V5 projects the original battle binding onto the unchanged detailed surface, retaining the independently measured rigid face core. Original battle whole-body coverage was visually inspected. Requires exact reference replay, unchanged sculpt/rig/curves/textures, independent face and whole-body validation, and actual candidate inspection before promotion. Candidate v5 rejected for 115 reference-transition warnings. V6 returns to measured separated face regions and diffuses the measured transition neighborhoods over connected UV seams, keeping rigid face vertices locked and feathering back to the untouched lower body below -0.60. Independent face, body and visual gates remain unchanged. Final broad-region gate rejected v9 because an abandoned v5 reference-transfer envelope remained registered over moving forearm vertex 20339 (visible-bind 0.0933, -0.1276, 0.7254). Restore the actual separated v6 repair regions plus the original upper-skull region for this gate. Frozen independent facial patches and full-body checks are unchanged. The repaired skin, sculpt and authored/reviewed motion must match v9 exactly; only the recipe metadata changes. Final review remains pending.

animationClearance.reason: The independently repaired rounded face intersects the authored raised sleeves during recoil. A focused ten-phase front/side visual experiment confirmed that reducing the head and upper-arm rotation excursions preserves a visible recoil while clearing the muzzle and cheeks. Key times, all other rotations, translations and scales remain authored.
